cases.prompt: We ship logs to Datadog and the collector cannot parse our pattern. Switch us to structured JSON, but keep local runs readable.
expectations: Uses logback-spring.xml rather than logback.xml because only the spring variant resolves springProfile and springProperty
Defines a pattern appender under a local or test profile and a LogstashEncoder appender under the negated profile
Escapes the ampersand in the negated profile name as & and explains the XML requirement
Sets a UTC time zone and custom service and environment fields derived from springProperty

cases.prompt: Sometimes our logs show the wrong tenant id, and only for requests that follow a specific one. Suspect the pooled thread.
expectations: Diagnoses MDC not being cleared on a reused request thread and requires MDC.clear in a finally block
States that MDC.clear is not MDC.remove of a single key, because every key set during the request must go
Warns that MDC does not propagate to an async executor without a ContextPropagatingTaskDecorator
Recommends an integration test that issues two requests with different tenants and asserts no cross-contamination

cases.prompt: Add a request id header we can grep for, because some log lines have no trace id.
expectations: Rejects generating a second correlation id while a trace exists and states the trace id is the join key
Requires the id to come from the Micrometer Tracing Span rather than a fresh random value
Allows a namespaced requestId only for work outside an observed request and requires it not to be labelled a trace id
Points out that lines without a trace id usually come from async, scheduled, or message work with lost context

cases.prompt: Our import job logs one line per row and the collector drops most of them. It also slowed the job down.
expectations: Replaces the per-row statement with one aggregate line carrying total, rejected, duration, and a bounded sample of ids
Points out the synchronous appender cost on the hot path and moves the appender behind a bounded AsyncAppender
Sets discardingThreshold and neverBlock explicitly and states which failure mode each choice accepts
Warns that low-level events are dropped silently at the default threshold and that the queue must be bounded to avoid an OOM

cases.prompt: Review this log statement: log.info("login for {} with token {} and body {}", email, request.getHeader("Authorization"), body);
expectations: Rejects logging the authorization header, the full request body, and the raw email
Requires the encoder-level redaction pattern as enforcement rather than reviewer discipline
Proposes a hashed or masked email and a token length or prefix, and a body size and hash instead of the body
Adds a test that scans captured output for known secret fixtures so a new key name is caught

cases.prompt: Turn on DEBUG for the repository package so we can see the SQL while we investigate a slow order.
expectations: Scopes the change to a single logger through the environment-variable relaxed binding name rather than the whole root level
Sets a bounded window and requires reverting in the same session, stating that a left-on DEBUG is an incident
Notes that org.hibernate.SQL is often better served by a statement inspector or a slow-query log than by application DEBUG
Keeps the production root at INFO and treats a level change as a capacity decision, not a debugging convenience
